findings.productVision: Every student who receives a lump-sum aid refund should feel calm confidence about money lasting the whole term — not a spreadsheet, but a quiet number they can trust. We are building the ambient 'term runway' layer for student finances: a passive tracker that paces a big refund into a per-week safe-to-spend figure, so students avoid the mid-term cash cliff without ever having to categorize a transaction. Grounded in user research showing anxiety drives avoidance of engagement-heavy budgeting tools, we win by being the lowest-touch, highest-trust way to make aid money last.
findings.positioningStatement: For financial-aid offices and the students they fund — who worry that lump-sum refunds run out before the term ends — the AI Expense Tracker is a passive term-runway tool that paces a refund into a weekly safe-to-spend number. Unlike YNAB (active envelope budgeting), Cleo (engagement-heavy chatbot), and Finny (education-first, not refund-paced), we are the only tool that natively treats a lump-sum aid refund as a depleting runway, delivered ambiently with zero daily categorization.
coreCompetencies: Refund-pacing engine: modeling a lump-sum aid disbursement across a known academic term into a rolling per-week safe-to-spend number that self-corrects with actual spend
Ambient/low-touch UX: surfacing one trustworthy number with near-zero required interaction, tuned against anxiety-avoidance behavior rather than for daily engagement
Passive bank-transaction ingestion and auto-classification good enough to require no manual categorization from the student
Institutional distribution and integration: onboarding via financial-aid offices, SSO/roster-aware deployment, admin-facing outcome reporting
Trust and security posture: SOC2 Type II compliance and student-data privacy as both deal prerequisite and brand pillar
Academic-calendar and aid-disbursement domain modeling (term boundaries, refund timing, mid-term gaps)

featurePriorityFramework.methodology: RICE, weighted toward impact on core anxiety/runway problem and institutional-deal readiness
criteria: Reach: students affected per term, weighted by institutional-channel leverage (features unlocking aid-office deals count higher than consumer-only reach)
Impact: direct effect on core problem — improves pacing accuracy, reduces mid-term cash-cliff risk, lowers engagement burden (scored 0.25/0.5/1/2/3)
Confidence: validation strength from upstream streams; unvalidated bundles (split, full budgeting) capped at low confidence
Effort: person-months, with explicit multiplier for anything touching SOC2 scope or institutional integration
Strategic gate (modifier): protects 18-24mo competitive window before agentic bank AI closes gap; avoids building commoditized capability others own (splitting owned by Splitwise)

evolutionBeyondMVP: Predictive shortfall alerts: warn ambiently when projected spend will exhaust runway before term end, with suggested weekly adjustment
Multi-refund / multi-term modeling: handle staggered disbursements, work-study income, multi-semester runway
Institutional analytics dashboard: aggregate (anonymized) outcome reporting for financial-aid offices to justify renewal/expansion
Student Plus tier depth: richer personalization, goal 'safety cushions', export — monetizing secondary Gen Z segment without compromising free-forever distribution asset
Aid-disbursement and SIS integrations (direct refund-schedule sync) to make pacing zero-setup at institutional scale

DEFERRED — expense splitting: explicitly NOT on the roadmap at launch or v2; Splitwise owns splitting and upstream flagged budget+split bundle as unconfirmed. Only revisit if a dedicated validation experiment proves it lifts core-runway retention.
